Govardovskii et al. (2000) visual-pigment template.

Source: R/species_perception.R
govardovskii_template.Rd

Reconstructs a photoreceptor's normalised absorbance spectrum from the peak wavelength alone, using the parametric template of Govardovskii et al. (2000) for A1 and A2 chromophores. This is the standard workhorse of comparative visual physiology.

Usage

govardovskii_template(lambda, lambda_max, chromophore = c("A1", "A2"))

Arguments

lambda

Wavelength grid in nm (numeric vector).

lambda_max

Peak absorbance wavelength in nm.

chromophore

Chromophore type: "A1" (11-cis retinal, default) or "A2" (11-cis 3,4-didehydroretinal). A2 shifts the peak toward longer wavelengths and broadens the spectrum.

Value

A data frame with columns lambda and S (normalised absorbance, 0–1).

Details

The template models absorbance as the sum of an \(\alpha\)-band (main peak) and a \(\beta\)-band (short-wavelength shoulder). The \(\alpha\)-band follows the four-parameter expression: $$S_\alpha(\lambda) = \left[ e^{A(a - x)} + e^{B(0.922 - x)} + e^{C(1.104 - x)} + D \right]^{-1}, \quad x = \frac{\lambda_{\max}}{\lambda}$$ where \(A\), \(B\), \(C\), \(D\), and \(a\) are chromophore-specific constants (A1: \(A=69.7\), \(B=28\), \(C=-14.9\), \(D=0.674\), \(a\) wavelength-dependent; A2: \(A=62.7\), \(B=26.5\), \(C=-15.6\), \(D=0.530\)). The \(\beta\)-band is a Gaussian: $$S_\beta(\lambda) = 0.26\,\exp\!\left[ -\!\left(\frac{\lambda - \lambda_\beta}{b}\right)^2 \right]$$ with \(\lambda_\beta = 189 + 0.315\,\lambda_{\max}\) and \(b = -40.5 + 0.195\,\lambda_{\max}\). The full template is \(S(\lambda) = \max(0,\, S_\alpha + S_\beta)\), normalised to a peak of 1.

References

Govardovskii VI, Fyhrquist N, Reuter T, Kuzmin DG, Donner K (2000) In search of the visual pigment template. Visual Neuroscience 17:509–528.

Examples

lam <- seq(300, 750, by = 1)
govardovskii_template(lam, lambda_max = 560)
